title: Aqueous Humour Production
description: This episode of Focus Cast by focuslinks opens the machinery behind the eye's quiet factory and teaches how aqueous humour is actually produced. Learn the three mechanisms and their shares: active secretion supplying roughly eighty to ninety percent, as fuel-burning pumps build a salt ridge between epithelial cells and water follows by osmosis, with carbonic anhydrase forging bicarbonate as a raw material; ultrafiltration adding a pressure-driven seep of plasma water across capillary walls, roughly a fifth; and simple diffusion contributing the sliver left. Hear the numbers in words: production at about two to three microlitres per minute in a young adult, a full renewal roughly every hundred minutes, and a normal circadian rhythm that lets the tap fall to roughly half during sleep. Understand why production depends on blood flow and on the epithelium's metabolic health, and why it is a controlled variable rather than a constant, a tap with the eye's own hand on the valve. Made for optometry students and practising optometrists who want normal ocular physiology explained for the ear.
